script.title: Decode letter codes with one rule
script.caption_hook: Crack any letter code in 10 seconds with this simple method

lines.say: Wait, how do people crack letter codes so fast?
Every code follows a fixed rule, which may have more than one step. Find it from one pair, then test every letter.

board.title: Decode Coding
board.sub: Find the rule, then test it

lines.say: Okay, but how do I find the rule?
Say CAT becomes FDW. Write places: 3, 1, 20 become 6, 4, 23. Every gap is plus three.
Yes, GRJ! That's a fixed shift. Common types: fixed shift, mirror, changing shift, reversal, and others.
A and Z are mirror twins. Their places always add to twenty-seven. So B pairs with Y.

board.title: Mirror Rule
board.sub: A=1, Z=26, so A-Z, B-Y, C-X

lines.say: What if the shift goes past Z?
Wrap around. Shift X by three: twenty-four plus three is twenty-seven. Subtract twenty-six and you get one, which is A.
So I test every letter, not just the first one?
Exactly! One pair shows the rule, all pairs prove it.
